product: miv-cel (mivocabtagene autoleucel, KYV-101), a fully human autologous CD19-targeting CAR T-cell therapy with CD28 co-stimulation given as a single dose to reset B cells; more than 100 autoimmune patients treated to date; three FDA RMAT designations in SPS, gMG and non-active secondary progressive MS.
demand: No FDA-approved therapy exists for stiff person syndrome, where roughly 6,000 US patients are diagnosed, and about 80,000 US patients have generalized myasthenia gravis; the company positions one dose as freeing patients from lifelong immunotherapy. Current demand is clinical-trial and named-patient access, not commercial sales.
pricing_power: Unproven. There is no approved product or revenue and no disclosed price; management argues SPS disease burden justifies a premium one-time price, and payer engagement is under way. Entrenched FcRn and complement drugs give reference pricing in gMG. Consensus models only 17.88 million dollars of revenue next year.
competition: Novartis rap-cel was halted after three participant deaths and Bristol Myers zola-cel enrollment was paused on 2026-08-31, removing two rivals but raising class-wide safety scrutiny. Other CD19 CAR-T autoimmune developers compete on durability and outpatient delivery, while FcRn inhibitors and complement drugs are entrenched in generalized myasthenia gravis.
team: CEO Warner Biddle; chief medical and development officer Naji Gehchan; chief technology officer Mayo Pujols; chief financial officer Greg Martini (2026-05-18); chief commercial officer Nadia Dac; chief legal and compliance officer Ritesh Srivastava (2026-06-22). The commercial and finance hires signal a deliberate commercial-stage transition.
market_strategy: Complete the rolling SPS BLA in Q4 2026 and seek priority review under RMAT for a 2027 launch, use SPS as the beachhead into generalized myasthenia gravis, non-active secondary progressive MS and broader neuroimmunology, and develop alternative or no-preconditioning outpatient regimens to widen access and defend a first-in-class position.
bull: 2026-09-24 KYSA-8 one-year data: 95% of SPS responders sustained benefit, 92% off immunotherapy, no high-grade CRS/ICANS; RMAT designations and rolling BLA with Q4 2026 completion target.
bear: Single-arm 26-patient SPS and 7-patient gMG cohorts, no control; cash fell to $199.4M at 2026-06-30 from $279.3M, net loss $38.3M, share count up to 61.8M; peer CAR-T deaths raise class safety bar.
falsifier: The rolling SPS BLA is not completed in Q4 2026, or the 2027 miv-cel launch slips past 2027-12-31.
web_what_changed: 2026-07-27 ElevateBio commercial manufacturing and supply agreement for miv-cel; 2026-08-11 Q2 2026 results with FDA RMAT designation in non-active secondary progressive MS, CMC module filed in the rolling SPS BLA, runway into 2028, new CFO CCO and legal chief; 2026-08-31 peers Novartis rap-cel halted after three deaths and Bristol Myers zola-cel paused; 2026-09-01 Kyverna safety statement; 2026-09-24 positive one-year KYSA-8 SPS data.
web_not_known_yesterday: 2026-09-24 one-year KYSA-8 data in 26 SPS patients: 95 percent of primary-analysis responders sustained benefit, 92 percent stayed off chronic immunotherapy, no high-grade CRS or ICANS and no IEC-HS; gMG Phase 2 follow-up extends to 1.5 years. New today is mainly the market reaction and confirmation the full dataset goes to ACTRIMS-ECTRIMS 2026-10-21 to 23 and AANEM 2026-09-29.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Pre-revenue, so no volume, price or mix exists yet. Growth potential is demand and indication expansion rather than price: single-dose miv-cel targets about 6,000 diagnosed US stiff person syndrome patients with no approved therapy and about 80,000 US generalized myasthenia gravis patients. First revenue depends on a possible 2027 SPS launch.
web_suppliers: ElevateBio is the announced CDMO for US commercial and global clinical miv-cel supply (2026-07-27), with company-claimed clinical manufacturing success above 98 percent; no other suppliers appear in the filings read. Manufacturing scale is the recognized class constraint. Kyverna also depends on a prospective NIH exclusive patent license for anti-CD19 CAR technology commented on 2026.
web_customers: No commercial customers; Kyverna is pre-revenue. The relevant customer set is payers, treatment centers and patients, and commercialization is only now being built (chief commercial officer, commercial site activation, payer and patient advocacy engagement, commercial supply agreement). No customer concentration can be measured today.
web_who_loses: Incumbent symptom and immunosuppressive therapy loses: IVIg, rituximab, plasmapheresis and steroids, plus FcRn and complement players such as argenx and UCB in myasthenia gravis. Rival autoimmune CAR-T developers lose relative position, notably Novartis rap-cel (halted) and Bristol Myers zola-cel (paused), and the first-approval race tightens if miv-cel wins.
web_contradicting_evidence: Single-arm open-label trials with tiny cohorts (26 SPS, 7 gMG) and no control arm, so durability rests on small samples. Cash fell to 199.4 million dollars at 2026-06-30 from 279.3 million; quarterly net loss 38.3 million; shares rose from 43.2 million to 61.8 million in a year via ATM and the December 2025 offering. G and A up 72 percent year over year. Price near 7 dollars versus a 30.40 dollar mean target signals market disbelief.
web_if_management_right: The rolling SPS BLA completes in Q4 2026, priority review follows the RMAT designations, miv-cel becomes the first FDA-approved CAR T for an autoimmune disease and the first approved SPS therapy, launching in 2027. gMG Phase 3 enrollment finishes mid-2027, the progressive MS strategy lands by early 2027, and outpatient or no-preconditioning regimens widen access on runway into 2028.
web_if_management_wrong: Durability fades or CMC and FDA requirements push the BLA past Q4 2026 and the 2027 launch slips. A funding gap opens: only 199.4 million dollars of cash at 2026-06-30, a 24.9 million dollar term loan and no revenue, so another equity raise and further dilution follow while commercial build costs keep running. Class-wide safety scrutiny after peer deaths raises the approval bar.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: ElevateBio as manufacturing partner; advanced-therapy tool, reagent and CDMO suppliers that scale CAR T; CROs and clinical sites running the KYSA trials plus the Stanford and UCSF investigator trials; outpatient infusion and apheresis networks; GAD65 antibody diagnostics; Oxford Finance as lender; and the wider autoimmune CAR-T field that gains from class validation.
